about: The God of Fire blend created by Carlos Fuente Sr., rolled by Arturo Fuente for Keith Park's Prometheus company. It is the medium-bodied counterpart to the Cameroon-wrapped by Carlito blend, and each band carries the year the cigars were made.
notes: Maker only says the wrapper is Ecuadorian. Halfwheel calls it Ecuadorian Sumatra; Corona Cigar lists Ecuadorian Habano. Maker calls it medium bodied, while retailers list medium-full to full. Made in small yearly batches; also sold as a Robusto Tubo.

about: The God of Fire blend created by Carlos "Carlito" Fuente Jr., rolled by Arturo Fuente for Keith Park's Prometheus company. The maker calls it the boldest God of Fire, with a Cameroon wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
notes: Maker describes it as medium to heavy; Corona Cigar and Neptune call it full. Made in small yearly batches with the production year on the second band. Halfwheel lists the Diademas 56 at 5 3/4 x 56; the maker lists 6 1/4 x 56.
verifyNotes: Removed 'leather' from flavors (not in any page opened) and added 'coffee' from Corona Cigar's notes. Note reworded: halfwheel lists, rather than measured, the Diademas 56 at 5 3/4 x 56.

wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro (Double Robusto, Gran Toro, Diademas 56) or Ecuadorian Sun Grown (Robusto, Robusto Gordo 54)
wrapperOrigin: USA or Ecuador, depending on size
about: A darker-wrapped God of Fire line rolled by Arturo Fuente for Prometheus, added in 2011. The wrapper depends on the size: Connecticut Broadleaf maduro on some, Ecuadorian sun grown on others, all over Dominican binder and filler.
notes: Two wrappers in one line, so check the size: Robusto and Robusto Gordo 54 are Ecuadorian Sun Grown, the others Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro. Maker gives no strength rating; halfwheel found it medium to medium-full and Corona Cigar lists full. Made in small yearly batches.
verifyNotes: Note corrected: no retailer opened says medium-plus. Halfwheel's review runs medium to medium-full and Corona Cigar lists full for both wrappers. Strength kept at Medium-Full on halfwheel's wording; the maker gives no rating.

about: The mildest of Gran Habano's three core blends from the Rico family, rolled at their factory in Danli, Honduras. A Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
notes: Maker only says Connecticut wrapper. Holt's lists it as Ecuador-grown Connecticut and Neptune as USA Connecticut Shade, so the origin is left blank. Maker rates it mild; Holt's says mild-medium and Neptune medium. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

Factory name is not on the maker or Holt's pages; confirmed from halfwheel, which names Gran Habano's Honduras factory as G.R. Tabacaleras Unidas S.A., and swapped that page in as a source. Danli is from the maker's About page.

about: The middle of Gran Habano's three core blends, which the Rico family calls its classic blend. A Nicaraguan Habano wrapper and binder over Nicaraguan, Mexican and Costa Rican filler, rolled in Danli, Honduras.
notes: Maker's spec line and Holt's say medium to full, but the maker's own description and Neptune call it medium. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

Danli is from the maker's About page.

about: The strongest of Gran Habano's three core blends, with a reddish Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper and a full, spicy profile. Rolled by the Rico family in Danli, Honduras.
notes: Maker lists about 15 sizes, including a 7 x 70 Grandioso; 10 of them are listed here. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

about: The maduro version of Gran Habano's full-bodied Corojo #5, with a dark sun-grown Nicaraguan wrapper over the same Nicaraguan and Costa Rican filler. Rolled at the Rico family's factory in Danli, Honduras.
notes: Maker lists a Nicaraguan Habano binder; halfwheel reported in 2015 that wrapper and binder are Nicaraguan Corojo, and Neptune lists a Costa Rican binder. Launch year not found; it got new bands and boxes in 2015. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

about: A Gran Habano line released in 2016 whose name means the conquest, with sizes named after Columbus's three ships. A Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler from Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Colombia, sold in boxes of 24.
notes: Halfwheel lists the binder as Nicaraguan Corojo. Its reviewer found the cigar closer to medium than the maker's medium to full rating. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.
verifyNotes: Blend fields unchanged. about reworded to drop 'premium' and to say the name means the conquest, as halfwheel puts it.

about: A Connecticut-wrapped line from Gran Habano, shipped in late 2018 and sold in cedar sleeves. It was made to show a Connecticut cigar does not have to be mild.
notes: Maker lists Nicaraguan and Costa Rican filler; halfwheel and Neptune list Nicaraguan only. Maker now rates it medium, though it was announced as mild to medium. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

about: The original Graycliff blend and the company's first line, rolled at its factory in Nassau, Bahamas. Graycliff Cigar Company was started in 1997 by Enrico Garzaroli of the Graycliff hotel with Cuban blender Avelino Lara.
notes: Also called Graycliff Original. Maker publishes no blend. A 2011 Cigar Coop review and Cigars Direct both give an Indonesian wrapper but disagree on the filler. Graycliff reworked its blends and cut sizes in 2015, so the size list may be out of date. Sold as medium, though that review found it mild.

about: Graycliff's second line after the Red Label, properly called the Profesionale Series and commonly known as the Blue Label. It is rolled at the Graycliff factory in Nassau, Bahamas.
notes: Blue Label is the nickname for the Profesionale Series. Blend is from Neptune's listing; the maker publishes none. A 2007 review listed an Indonesian wrapper and binder with Brazilian, Nicaraguan and Honduran filler, so the blend has changed over time. Confirm against the box before quoting.

about: Introduced in late 2003 as the fullest-bodied Graycliff blend, created by Avelino Lara with owner Enrico Garzaroli. It is rolled in Nassau, Bahamas, with a dark, rough Costa Rican wrapper, and is also known as the Black Label.
notes: Binder is disputed: halfwheel says Cameroon, Corona Cigar says undisclosed and Cigars Direct lists Costa Rican. Halfwheel's reviewer found it nearer medium in strength. Other sizes such as the Elegante lancero were store exclusives. Do not confuse it with the separate Double Espresso line.
